p0.original: 关键问题：应激如何对我们的身体造成影响
p0.en: Key issue: How stress affects our bodies

p2.original: 身体的应激反应始于唤醒，唤醒会激发一系列生理反应。这些反应在短期内具有适应性，但如果持续时间过长，就会给个体带来伤害。
p2.en: The physical stress begins with a wake-up call that triggers a series of physical reactions. These responses are adaptive in the short term, but if they last too long, they can harm individuals.

p3.original: 自地球诞生之日起，在面对捕食者或敌对部落的致命打击时，人类为了生存必须做出快速而果断的反应。我们的祖先适应了世界各地迥异的自然环境条件，战胜了极端的气候、稀缺的资源和敌人。面对这些挑战时，迅速采取行动是必要的，只有这样才能获得庇护所、寻找食物并保护自己。一个人越能快速地感知到危险、准确地评估情况并采取适当的行动，他们生存并获得成功的机会就越大。在人类进化的过程中，那些对危险反应最快、最有效的个体存活了下来，并将这些基因遗传给了他们的后代，而反应慢或不太聪明的个体存活下来并繁衍后代的可能性较小。
p3.en: Since the birth of the planet, humanity has had to respond quickly and decisively to the deadly blows of predators or rival tribes in order to survive. Our ancestors have adapted to the diverse natural environment conditions around the world and have overcome extreme weather, scarce resources and enemies. In the face of these challenges, quick action is necessary in order to obtain shelter, find food and protect themselves. The more a person can quickly sense danger, accurately assess the situation and take appropriate action, the greater will be their chances of survival and success. In the process of human evolution, the most rapid and effective individuals who react to danger survive and pass on these genes to their descendants, while slow or less intelligent individuals are less likely to survive and reproduce.

p4.original: 我们的祖先面临的一些严重的应激源，如灾难或战争，如今依旧存在。当然，现代生活也增加了一些新的应激源：工作要求严格、财务上的担忧和计算机崩溃。这些新应激源通常是长期存在的，所以祖先们所采取的应对方式不一定适合我们。然而，我们的应激反应系统是进化而来的，因为人类的生理进化无法像社会发展那样快速。面对可怕或令人愤怒的情境时，远古的生物印迹体现在我们身体的自动反应中。如果有人侮辱你，你会感到脸发热，你的拳头似乎会不由自主地握紧，为身体的比拼做好准备。或者想象另一种迥然不同的“威胁”：在课堂讨论中老师点名让你发言，而你却没有准备，你的心跳加速，双膝颤抖，有种想要逃跑的冲动。
p4.en: Some serious sources of stress for our ancestors, such as disasters or wars, still exist today. Of course, modern life has also added a number of new sources of stress: stringent work requirements, financial concerns and computer collapse. These new sources of stress are usually long-term, so the response of the ancestors is not necessarily appropriate for us. However, our stress systems have evolved, because the physical evolution of humankind cannot be as rapid as that of social development. In the face of terrible or angry circumstances, ancient biological traces are reflected in the automatic reaction of our bodies. If someone insults you, you'll feel the heat, and your fists will seem to be squeezing and preparing for the body fight. Or imagine another very different “threat”: the teacher who calls you to speak in class discussions without you being prepared, your heart beats faster, your knees trembles, and you have an urge to escape.

p5.original: 这些例子说明了战斗或逃跑反应（fight-or-flight response）的两个极端，这是当生物体感知到威胁时会触发的一系列内在和行为过程，以便为战斗或逃跑做好准备。这种反应对我们的祖先而言非常有效，但并不总是适合今天的我们。毕竟逃跑不是应对课堂发言的有效方法。这一学习阶段的核心概念总结了这一点：
p5.en: These examples illustrate two extremes of combat-or-flight response, a series of inherent and behavioural processes that are triggered when a biological body perceives a threat in order to prepare for combat or escape. This response has been very effective for our ancestors, but it has not always been appropriate for us today. After all, running away is not an effective way of responding to class statements. This is summarized in the core concept of this learning phase:

p6.original: 身体的应激反应始于唤醒，唤醒会激发一系列生理反应。这些反应在短期内具有适应性，但如果持续时间过长，就会给个体带来伤害。
p6.en: The physical stress begins with a wake-up call that triggers a series of physical reactions. These responses are adaptive in the short term, but if they last too long, they can harm individuals.

p7.original: 令人惊讶的是，我们大多数时候都能有效地应对应激，不仅能保持健康，甚至还能体验到快乐。但是，正如你在这一学习阶段中将看到的，如果我们不能有效地应对应激，无论应激是由什么造成的，都会引发严重的后果。从积极的方面来看，需要强调的是，通常应激带来的情绪唤醒对我们是有利的：我们的注意力会因此集中在威胁事件上，并做好应对的准备。从消极的方面来看，极端或长期的情绪唤醒会威胁我们的健康，引发一些疾病，如心脏病、中风、高血压和溃疡。我们的心理健康也会受到影响。
p7.en: Surprisingly, most of the time we can respond effectively to stress, not only to maintain health, but also to experience happiness. But, as you will see at this learning stage, if we do not respond effectively to stress, whatever the consequences of it are, there are serious consequences. On the positive side, it needs to be emphasized that it is in our interest to awaken the emotions that usually result from stress: thus, our attention will be focused on the threat events and will be prepared to respond. On the negative side, extreme or long-term emotional awakening threatens our health and causes diseases such as heart disease, stroke, hypertension and ulcer. Our mental health will also be affected.

p8.original: 有些人总是担心自己生病，总觉得会发生不好的事情，从轻微的刺激到重大的创伤（Sapolsky，1994）。抑郁症、创伤后应激障碍和其他焦虑症都与应激有直接关联。这些问题不仅会出现在救援人员和空中交通管制员身上，在公共部门和私营部门的各级员工及各行各业、各个年龄段的人身上也会出现。让我们仔细地了解应激反应的生理机制，这有助于我们清楚地意识到，当长期应激削弱我们有限的资源时，这种适应性反应如何引发了消极的健康后果。
p8.en: Some people are always worried about their illness and think that something bad is going to happen, ranging from mild irritation to major trauma (Sapolsky, 1994). Depression, post-traumatic stress disorder and other anxiety disorders are all directly related to stress. These problems arise not only with rescue workers and air traffic controllers, but also with employees at all levels and in all walks of life, in both the public and private sectors. Let us be careful about the physiological mechanisms of stress, which helps us to understand clearly how this adaptive response can have negative health consequences when long-term stress weakens our limited resources.

p10.en: 14.3 Describe the physiological response to stress.

p11.original: 14.4 探讨应激对免疫系统的负面影响。
p11.en: 14.4 Explore the negative impact of stress on the immune system.

p14.en: Describe the physical response to stress.

p15.original: 通常消防员会说他们热爱自己的工作，对于有些人来说，这份工作是一种家族传承的职业。但是，当他们响应警报、冲向危险时，这些战友情谊和奉献精神并不能降低受伤和死亡的风险，减少他们所经历的应激水平。一个有经验的消防员的身体对应激源是如何做出反应的呢？你的身体对应激又是如何做出反应的呢？
p15.en: Firefighters usually say they love their work, which is, for some, a family-based occupation. However, when they respond to warnings and rush to danger, these comradeships and dedication do not reduce the risk of injury and death and the level of stress they experience. How does an experienced fireman's body respond to stress? And how does your body react?

p17.original: 当一个令人紧张的情境突然出现时，比如当消防员第一次听到警报时，应激反应就开始了，自主神经系统（autonomic nervous system，ANS）产生突然且强烈的生理唤醒。生理唤醒的特征包括心跳加速、呼吸加快、血压升高和大量出汗。在这个情境中出现的系列反应都属于急性应激（acute stress）。它是由应激源引发的临时唤醒模式，有明显的发作点和有限的持续时间。在一个世纪前，生理学家沃尔特·坎农（Walter Cannon）首次描述了这种应激（1914）。
p17.en: When a stressful situation emerges, such as when firefighters first hear the alarm, the stress starts, and the autonomous nervous system (autonomic nervous system, ANS) produces sudden and intense physical awakening. Characteristics of physical awakening include an acceleration of the heart rate, an acceleration of the breathing rate, increased blood pressure and extensive sweating. The series of reactions in this situation is classified as acute stress. It is a form of temporary awakening triggered by stress, with clear onset and limited duration. A century ago, Walter Cannon, the physiologist, first described the stress (1914).

p18.original: 几乎是一瞬间，我们的神经系统、内分泌系统和肌肉会促使我们做出有效的反应，在有需要时给予我们额外的力量。图14-4详细展示了当有应激反应时，身体采取的多种行动。
p18.en: Almost for a moment, our nervous system, endocrine system and muscles will prompt us to react effectively and give us additional force when needed. Figure 14-4 provides a detailed picture of the various actions taken by the body when there is stress.

p19.original: 图14-4 身体对应激的各种反应

p20.original: 注：在急性应激情况下，身体会产生一系列惊人的生理反应以让我们做好战斗或逃跑的准备。
p20.en: Note: In acute stress, the body produces a series of alarming physical reactions to prepare us for combat or escape.

p21.original: 当你需要逃离火灾现场，面对敌人或躲避迎面而来的汽车而急转弯时，战斗或逃跑反应可以成为你的救星。然而当面对长期的应激时，这种反应是有代价的：在生理上对威胁一直保持警惕，最终会损耗身体的自然防御系统。因此，频繁面对应激或经常把经历的事件解释为应激会给个体的健康带来严重的风险：原本健康的应激反应可能会危害健康。在下面的内容中，我们将详细探讨这种情况是如何发生及为什么会发生。
p21.en: When you need to flee the fire scene and turn in the face of the enemy or of the incoming car, fighting or running away can be your salvation. However, in the face of long-term stress, there is a cost in this response: physical vigilance over threats can ultimately deplete the body's natural defence system. Therefore, frequent exposure to stress or frequent interpretation of events experienced can be interpreted as a serious risk to an individual's health: an already healthy stress can be harmful to health. In the following section, we will look at how and why this happened.

p22.original: 图中的女性正在面临一个急性应激情况。她所居住的村庄附近发生了森林火灾，对她的家造成了威胁，应激源突然出现了，应激反应始于突然的、强烈的生理唤醒。
p22.en: The women in the figure are facing an acute stress situation. The forest fires near the village in which she lived posed a threat to her home, and the sources of stress suddenly appeared, which began with a sudden, intense physical awakening.

p24.original: 20世纪中叶，得益于加拿大内分泌学家汉斯·塞里（Hans Selye）的研究，我们开始理解应激是如何导致疾病的。简而言之，塞里（Selye，1956，1991）发现，不同的应激源会触发本质上相同的系统反应或一般的身体反应，为了应对威胁而调动身体资源。此外，他还发现所有的应激源都会促使身体进行适应或调整。由于身体的反应是一般性的，并非针对特定的应激源，塞里将其称为一般适应性综合征（general adaptation syndrome，GAS，见图14-5）。
p24.en: In the middle of the twentieth century, thanks to research by the Canadian endocrine scientist Hans Serye, we began to understand how stress caused disease. In short, Selye, 1956, 1991 found that different sources of stress trigger essentially the same systemic or general physical response, mobilizing physical resources to respond to threats. In addition, he found that all the stressors would induce the body to adapt or adjust. As the physical response is general and not directed at specific stressors, it is referred to by Serry as a general adaptive syndrome (general adaptation syndrome, GAS, see figure 14-5).

p25.original: 图14-5 一般适应性综合征

p26.original: 在急性应激情况下，这些反应会帮助我们生存和成长，但如果长期处于高水平应激状态，便会引发心脏病、哮喘、头痛、胃溃疡、关节炎等其他疾病（Carlson，2007；Salovey et al.，2000）。塞里的一般适应性综合征模型对威胁的三阶段反应进行了描述，包括警觉阶段、抵抗阶段和衰竭阶段（Johnson，1991；Selye，1956，1991）。
p26.en: In acute stress, these responses help us to survive and grow, but if a high level of stress persists, other diseases such as heart disease, asthma, headache, stomach ulcer, arthritis, etc. (Carlson, 2007); Salovy et al., 2000. The general adaptive syndrome model of Serry describes the three-stage response to the threat, including the alert phase, the resistance phase and the failure phase (Johnson, 1991); Seelye, 1956, 1991.

p28.original: 在应激的第一阶段，身体激活了警报系统并开始调动资源来对抗应激源。塞里称第一阶段为警觉阶段（alarm phase）。这与坎农所说的战斗或逃跑反应类似。下丘脑（hypothalamus）会同时释放两条紧急消息。其中一条消息通过图14-6所示的途径向激素系统（特别是肾上腺）发出信号，由此大量类固醇激素进入血液。这类化学物质能够提升力量和耐力（这就是一些运动员冒险滥用类固醇的原因）。大脑也会释放内啡肽，减少身体对疼痛的感知。与此同时，另一条消息通过自主神经系统的交感神经（sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system）被传递到内部器官和腺体，唤醒身体采取行动。
p28.en: During the first phase of stress, the body activated the alarm system and began to mobilize resources to counter the stressors. Seri called the first phase a alert phase (alarm case). This is similar to what Canon described as a response to combat or escape. Two urgent messages will be released at the same time by hypothalamus. One of the messages sent signals to the hormone system (especially adrenal gland) through the routes shown in figures 14-6, which resulted in large quantities of steroid hormones entering the blood. Such chemicals can increase strength and tolerance (this is why some athletes risk misuse of steroids). The brain also releases endorphins and reduces the body's perception of pain. At the same time, another message was transmitted to internal organs and gland bodies through the sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system to alert the body to action.

p29.original: 图14-6 警觉阶段的激素反应
p29.en: Figure 14-6: Hormonal response in the alert phase

p30.original: 注：在一般适应性综合征的警觉阶段，激素系统反应是由下丘脑同时触发的两条反应通路中的其中一条通路。
p30.en: Note: During the alert phase of the General Adaptive Syndrome, the hormone system reaction is one of two reaction routes that are simultaneously triggered by the hypothalamus.

p31.original: 正是通过交感神经系统和内分泌系统这两条通路传递的消息，我们做好了行动的准备。更多的血液流向心脏、大脑和肌肉，使我们思考和反应的更好、更快。相反，流入消化系统的血液减少，这样我们的身体在紧急情况下就不会把宝贵的能量消耗在非必要的功能上。我们的瞳孔放大，周边视野扩大，为防止身体过热而大量排汗。血糖含量也会增加，为身体提供额外的能量。总而言之，我们的身体对眼前的危险高度敏感。图14-7详细列出了一系列自主反应。
p31.en: It is through these two pathways of synergetic nervous and endocrine systems that we are ready to act. More blood flows to the heart, the brain and the muscles, making us think and react better and faster. On the contrary, the flow of blood into the digestive system is reduced so that our bodies do not consume valuable energy in non-essential functions in emergency situations. Our pupils are amplified, our horizons are expanded, and we are sweating heavily to prevent overheating. Blood sugar levels will also increase, providing additional energy to the body. In short, our bodies are highly sensitive to the immediate danger. Figure 14-7 details a range of autonomous responses.

p32.original: 图14-7 警觉阶段的交感神经系统反应
p32.en: Figure 14-7. Perceptive nervous system response during alert phase

p33.original: 注：这张图展示了交感神经系统对急性应激的反应通路，它与激素系统反应平行发生。
p33.en: Note: This chart shows the reaction path of the intersectional nervous system to acute stress, which occurs in parallel with the hormonal system.

p34.original: 警觉阶段的功能是使有机体能够抵抗或逃离威胁，这个阶段对于我们的祖先而言通常不会持续很长时间。然而，考虑到现代应激具有长期性的特点，我们通常会进入第二阶段——抵抗阶段。
p34.en: The vigilance phase, which enables organisms to resist or escape threats, usually does not last long for our ancestors. However, given the long-term nature of modern stress, we usually move into the second phase — resistance.

p36.original: 如果应激源长期存在——但强度没有第一阶段那么强烈，我们便进入了抵抗阶段（resistance phase）。在此期间，警觉阶段的所有生理变化仍然存在。在抵抗阶段，身体试图抵抗应激源带来的影响。免疫系统不停地高速运转，白细胞数量增加，以有助于身体抵抗感染。
p36.en: If the source of stress persists — but not as strong as the first phase — we enter the resistance phase. During this period, all physical changes in the alert phase remain. During the resistance phase, the body tried to resist the effects of the stressors. The immune system is operating at constant high speed and the number of white cells is increasing to help the body resist infection.

p37.original: 令人惊讶的是，这一阶段的抵抗只适用于原始的应激源。塞里的研究发现，如果动物在实验中已经适应了一个应激源（如电击），那么当加入了第二个应激源（如极度寒冷）时，动物很快就会死亡。很显然动物的资源已经衰竭了，它们无法调动资源以抵抗新的应激源。类似的悲剧也会出现在人类身上，一名士兵在经历了几个月的紧张战斗之后，无法应对战俘营中的新应激，很快就死亡了。
p37.en: Surprisingly, resistance at this stage only applies to the original source of stress. Serry found that if animals have adapted to one source of stress (e.g. electric shocks) in the experiment, then animals will die very soon when a second source of stress (e.g. extreme cold) is added. It is clear that the resources of animals have been depleted and that they are unable to mobilize resources to counter new sources of stress. A similar tragedy will occur to humanity, where a soldier, after several months of intense fighting, was unable to cope with the new stress in the camp and died very soon.

p38.original: 因此，我们看到，在警觉和抵抗阶段，个体为了抵抗应激源需要使用身体的能量。这减少了个体应对额外应激时的可用资源。例如，想象一下这样一个场景：期末考试刚刚结束，为了应对考试，考试前一周你每天都夜以继日地学习，睡眠不足，靠垃圾食品和咖啡度日。考试终于结束了，你可以放松和休息了，但是电话响了：电话那头传来了恋人的声音，并且透露出消极的情绪。还没等你宣布自己终于完成考试的好消息，恋人却说：“我不知道该怎么对你说，但是，我们必须谈谈……”这可能不是好消息，甚至可能意味着严重的问题，如分手。这绝对是一个应激源。已经被刚过去一周的压力搞得筋疲力尽的你，将如何处理这场重要的谈话呢？你感到无所适从、害怕，甚至内心充满了愤怒：怎么会这样？为什么是这个时候？因为你的防御系统资源已经被耗尽了，你可能会反应过度，发现自己缺乏足够的认知和情感资源来有效地处理这种情况。
p38.en: Thus, we see that at the alert and resistance stage, individuals need to use their body energy in order to resist stressors. This reduces the resources available for individual responses to additional stress. Imagine, for example, that the final exam has just been completed and that in order to cope with it, you study day and night every week before the examination, you are not sleeping enough and you live on junk food and coffee. The exam is finally over, you can relax and rest, but the phone rings: the phone's got a lover's voice and negative emotions. Before you announce the good news that you have finally finished the exam, the lover says, “I don't know what to say to you, but we have to talk about it...” This may not be good news, and it may even mean serious problems, such as breaking up. This is definitely a source of stress. How will you deal with this important conversation when you've been exhausted by the stress of the past week? You feel helpless, afraid, even angry inside: how? Why this time? Because your defence system resources have been exhausted, you may overreact and find yourself lacking sufficient cognitive and emotional resources to deal effectively with the situation.

p40.original: 抵抗阶段是身体对抗应激源的最后努力，如果充满应激的情境在这个阶段依然没有得到改善，身体便无法继续这种激烈的生理战斗了。在第三阶段——衰竭阶段（exhaustion phase），身体机能恢复到正常范围，然后跌至正常水平以下。此时，身体需要休息和恢复活力，以便我们的生理功能升到可接受的水平。如果身体得不到必需的喘息，就像现在面临各种长期应激源一样，前两个阶段具有适应性的反应会使得身体在第三阶段面临生病的风险。
p40.en: The resistance stage is the last effort of the body to counter the stressors, and the body cannot continue this intense physical battle if the stressful situation remains unaltered at this stage. In the third phase - exhaustion phase (exhaustion case), the body function is restored to normal range and then below normal level. At this point, the body needs to rest and rejuvenate so that our biological function can rise to acceptable levels. If the body does not get the required breathing, as is now the case with long-term stressors, adaptive responses from the first two phases expose the body to the risk of illness in the third phase.

p41.original: 在衰竭阶段，身体的一些反应过程可能导致个体的身体和精神状况恶化。例如，血压升高在短期内会导个体头痛，血压长期升高会导致个体中风和得冠心病，这是导致死亡的两个主要原因。与此同时，消化系统受损会导致某些类型的溃疡，长此以往还会导致肥胖。长期应激还会增加血液中的脂肪堆积，从而增加中风的风险。在衰竭的免疫系统中还潜伏着其他危险，使得压力大的人更有可能被感染或患上其他疾病。此外，长时间持续或重复出现的应激可能会在大脑中产生长期的改变，从而引发抑郁症（Sapolsky，1998；Schulkin，1994）。应激激素还会作用于大脑，干扰其神经元再生的能力，尤其是海马中的神经元（Gould et al.，1998；Sapolsky，1998）。这就解释了为什么长时间使用类固醇（实际上是应激激素）是危险的（除非在某些医疗条件下使用）：类固醇的长期使用会让身体处于一般适应性综合征的最后一个阶段，即衰竭阶段，从而产生恶化的危险。
p41.en: At the stage of failure, some physical reaction processes may lead to the deterioration of an individual's physical and mental state. For example, rising blood pressure causes individual headaches in the short term, and long-term increases in blood pressure lead to individual strokes and coronary heart disease, which are the two main causes of death. At the same time, impairment of the digestive system can lead to certain types of ulcer, which in the long run also leads to obesity. Long-term stress also increases the accumulation of fat in blood, increasing the risk of strokes. Other risks are also present in the failing immune system, which increases the risk that people under stress will be infected or suffer from other diseases. In addition, persistent or repeated stress over a long period of time may cause long-term brain changes that can lead to depression (Sapolsky, 1998); Schulkin, 1994. The hormone also acts on the brain and interferes with its ability to regenerate neurons, especially in sea horses (Gould et al., 1998); Sapolsky, 1998. This explains why the long-term use of steroids (which are in fact hormones) is dangerous (unless used under certain medical conditions): long-term use of steroids can put the body at the last stage of general adaptive syndrome, namely, the stage of failure, and thus the risk of deterioration.

p42.original: 因此，塞里的一般适应性综合征模型解释了应激不仅会导致最初的战斗或逃跑反应，还会导致慢性疾病，并且使人变得衰弱。虽然新的研究表明，并不是所有的应激都会使内分泌系统产生完全相同的反应（Kemeny，2003），但这个模型仍然被广泛接受，并被认为是理解应激和疾病之间联系的关键。在深入探讨长期应激反应之前，我们首先要考虑战斗或逃跑反应的一个有趣的替代选项：养育。
p42.en: Therefore, the general adaptive syndrome model in Serry explains that stress can lead not only to initial combat or escape reactions, but also to chronic diseases and weakens people. While new studies have shown that not all stress causes the endocrine system to react exactly the same (Kemeny, 2003), the model is still widely accepted and is considered key to understanding the link between stress and disease. Before we go into the long-term stress, we should first consider an interesting alternative to combat or escape response: parenting.

p44.original: 心理学家谢莉·泰勒（Shelley Taylor）指出，战斗或逃跑模型是由男性理论家在研究雄性被试（雄性老鼠和男性）时发展出来的。泰勒注意到，在战斗或逃跑模型中，恐惧和攻击性非常突出，而这两者更多地反映的是男性的特征（Taylor，2003；Taylor et al.，2000b）。互助友好模型（tend-and-befriend）或许能更好地解释女性在自身或子女面临威胁时采取的行为。泰勒的理论认为，由于女性是子女的主要照料者，从生物学角度看，女性优先考虑保护子女的生命。从这个角度来看，战斗或逃跑是没有意义的。攻击性（“战斗”）会对自己或孩子造成伤害，逃跑会使孩子们毫无防备。从女性作为照料者的角度看，这两种反应对适应和生存都没有助益（Volpe，2004）。
p44.en: Shelly Taylor, a psychologist, stated that models of combat or escape had been developed by male theorists in their research into males being tested (male rats and males). Taylor noted that fear and aggression were prominent in combat or escape models, both of which reflected more male characteristics (Taylor, 2003); Taylor et al., 2000b. The "Tend-and-befriend" model may better explain the behaviour of women when they are threatened by themselves or their children. Taylor's theory suggests that, as women are the primary caregivers of children, women give priority to protecting their lives from a biological standpoint. From this perspective, fighting or running away is meaningless. An offensive (“combat”) can cause harm to itself or to the children, and running away can leave the children unprotected. From the point of view of women as caregivers, both responses are not helpful for adaptation and survival (Volpe, 2004).

p45.original: 互助友好模型认为，从生理上讲，女性倾向于通过照顾和保护子女以应对威胁，这种反应得到大脑和激素活动的支持。寻求社会支持创建了网络，这增强个人保护和照顾子女的能力（Eisler & Levine，2002；Taylor et al.，2000b）。在一项支持互助友好模型的研究中，检测了男性和女性在一次重要的考试前的激素变化和自我报告的焦虑水平。虽然在焦虑水平上男女的报告没有差异，但男性的皮质醇（cortisol）水平明显高于女性（Ennis et al.，2001）。另外有研究表明，另一种应激激素催产素（oxytocin）与女性的雌激素结合，促进了寻求归属行为（Taylor，2009）。较高的催产素水平也与镇静和更少的焦虑有关，这是有效养育的重要组成部分。
p45.en: The Mutual Assistance Model considers that, biologically, women tend to respond to threats by caring for and protecting their children, a response supported by brain and hormone activity. The creation of a network for social support, which empowers individuals to protect and care for their children (Eisler & Levine, 2002); Taylor et al., 2000b. In a study to support mutual friendship models, hormone changes and self-reported anxiety levels among men and women before a major examination were tested. Although there are no differences between the levels of anxiety reported by men and women, the level of cortisol is significantly higher for men than for women (Ennis et al., 2001). There are also studies that show that another form of oxytocin combines with female estrogen, facilitating the search for attribution (Taylor, 2009). Higher levels of oxytocin are also associated with calm and less anxiety, which is an important component of effective parenting.

p46.original: 令人惊讶的或许是，无论男性还是女性，都将寻求社会支持视为一种应激反应，虽然目前的证据表明，女性比男性更频繁、更稳定地采用这种方式（Tamres et al.，2002）。例如，对于患有早期乳腺癌的女性来说，来自伴侣的情感支持能够缓解她们每天的应激（Gilmore et al.，2011）。但重要的是，随着身体疼痛程度的增加，她们对伴侣支持的需要也在增加。研究人员敦促伴侣要理解这种不断增加的需要，并且尽可能提供这种支持，而不是变得沮丧甚至放弃。这样做对伴侣自身的健康可能也是有利的。研究表明，向朋友、亲戚和邻居提供帮助和情感支持的老年人的死亡率更低（Brown et al.，2003）。
p46.en: It may be surprising that the search for social support, whether male or female, is seen as a form of stress, although current evidence suggests that women use this method more frequently and steadily than men (Tamres et al., 2002). For example, emotional support from a partner can alleviate the daily stress for women with early breast cancer (Gilmore et al., 2011). However, it is important that as the level of physical pain increases, so does their need for partner support. Researchers urge partners to understand this growing need and to provide such support to the extent possible, rather than becoming frustrated or even giving up. This may also be beneficial to the partner's own health. Studies have shown that older persons who provide help and emotional support to friends, relatives and neighbours have lower mortality rates (Brown et al., 2003).

p47.original: 这些互补的应激反应——战斗或逃跑和互助友好——是一种比我们之前认为的更复杂的应激反应。我们看到应激系统在不断发展，这使我们在面临危险时既能保护自己，又能向他人伸出援手（Pitman，2003）。互助友好模型有力地补充了战斗或逃跑模型，两者的共同作用不仅有利于个人的生存，对人际关系和群体的生存也是一种保障。
p47.en: These complementary stressors — combat or escape and mutual friendship — are more complex than we thought before. We have seen the continuous development of stress systems, which allow us to protect ourselves and to reach out to others when we are at risk (Pitman, 2003). The mutual friendship model is a powerful complement to the model of combat or escape, and its combined effect not only serves the survival of individuals, but also guarantees interpersonal relations and group survival.

p50.original: 探讨应激对免疫系统的负面影响。
p50.en: Explore the negative impact of stress on the immune system.

p51.original: 在前文，我们指出在处于一般适应性综合征的衰竭阶段时，免疫系统在面对应激时变得特别脆弱。例如，研究表明，在面对伴侣死亡或一段重要的长期关系结束时，当事人经常会出现抑郁和免疫抑制（immunosuppression），这使他们特别容易患病（Cohen & Syme，1985；Kiecolt-Glaser & Glaser，1987，2001）。
p51.en: As noted earlier, the immune system becomes particularly vulnerable in the face of stress when it is at the stage of failure of a general adaptive syndrome. For example, studies have shown that at the end of a partner's death or an important long-term relationship, the person in question often suffers from depression and immunosuppression, which makes them particularly vulnerable to disease (Cohen & Syme, 1985); Kiecolt-Glaser & Glaser, 1987, 2001.

p53.original: 近年来，激发了一个因生物技术的进步而得以发展的令人兴奋的新领域，这个新领域试图寻找应激导致疾病的原因。心理神经免疫学（psycho-neuroimmunology）汇聚了心理学、神经科学和免疫学这三个领域。心理学家研究影响应激的心理因素，包括认知和情绪；神经科学家研究大脑功能；免疫学家对免疫系统有广泛的了解。虽然这个领域有着令人印象深刻的长名称，但它对身心联系的兴趣并不新鲜。两千多年前，古希腊人和古代中国人就已经在宗教研究中对心理神经免疫学的问题进行了探讨。
p53.en: In recent years, an exciting new area that has been developed as a result of advances in biotechnology has sought to identify the causes of stress that have led to disease. Psychoneurological immunology (psycho-neuromunology) brings together the three fields of psychology, neuroscience and immunology. Psychologists study the psychological factors influencing stress, including cognitive and emotional factors; Research on brain functions by neuroscientists; Immunologists have a wide understanding of the immune system. Although this area has impressive long names, its interest in physical and mental contact is not new. More than 2,000 years ago, ancient Greeks and ancient Chinese had explored the issue of psycho-neurological immunology in religious studies.

p54.original: 14.4.2 大脑和身体的双向联系
p54.en: 14.4.2 Two-way link between brain and body

p55.original: 对心理过程和免疫过程是如何相互影响的，以及外部社会对它们造成的影响进行研究，是心理神经免疫学的一个主要目标。这个任务的基础是大脑和身体能够以双向的方式交流（Maier & Watkins，1999）。例如，当人们感受到压力时，大脑会向肾上腺发出信号，促使它分泌一种主要的应激激素——皮质醇。随后大脑收到皮质醇传回的信号，并调节自身的分泌（Maier & Watkins，2000）。心理应激也会激活免疫系统。大脑和免疫系统之间穿梭的化学物质是一种被称为细胞因子（cytokines）的蛋白质。细胞因子最有趣的一个方面是，它们会向中枢神经系统发射信号，引发行为改变，包括疲劳、发烧或社交回避等。这些改变有助于生物体从疾病或伤害中恢复过来，所以它们是有益的（DeAngelis，2002a）。然而，如果时间太长，那么这些变化会增加罹患抑郁症等疾病的风险。而且，我们再次看到了与一般适应性综合征相似的地方。
p55.en: A study of how psychological processes and immunization processes interact with each other and how they are affected by the outside community is a major objective of psycho-neurological immunisation. This task is based on the ability of the brain and body to communicate in a two-way manner (Maier & Watkins, 1999). For example, when people feel pressure, the brain sends a signal to the adrenal gland, prompting it to squirt a major stressor - cortex. The brain then receives a signal from the cortical alcohol and regulates its own genre (Maier & Watkins, 2000). Psychological stress also activates the immune system. The chemical substance that travels between the brain and the immune system is a protein known as cytokines. One of the most interesting aspects of the cytogens is that they send signals to the central nervous system and trigger behavioural changes, including fatigue, fever or social evasion. These changes help organisms recover from disease or injury, so they are beneficial (DeAngelis, 2002a). However, these changes increase the risk of diseases such as depression if they take too long. And again, we see a similarity to the general adaptive syndrome.

p56.original: 在研究大脑如何调节细胞因子对应激反应的最早研究中，心理学家乔治·斯拉维奇（George Slavich）要求被试在一群穿着白大褂的威严的评委面前做即兴演讲。结果与预期一致，人们的细胞因子水平在即兴演讲期间显著升高（Slavich et al.，2010b）。接下来，被试玩虚拟的投球游戏，在此过程中，另外两名玩家突然把被试排斥在外。之后，斯拉维奇扫描了这些被试的大脑，他同时检测了细胞因子和脑扫描数据，注意到对于遭遇排斥时大脑激活反应更强烈的人，在演讲中其细胞因子活动也更多。
p56.en: In the first study of how the brain regulates the cytogenic response to stress, the psychologist George Slavic called for improvisation in front of a group of powerful judges in white coats. The results were consistent with expectations, with a marked increase in the cytogen level during improvisation (Slavich et al., 2010b). Next, they tried to play a virtual pitch game, during which two other players suddenly excluded the test. Later, Slavic scanned these tested brains, and he tested both cytogens and brain scans, noting that there were more cytological activity in the speech for those who responded more strongly to brain activation in the event of exclusion.

p57.original: 从这些结果中，我们能得到什么结论？
p57.en: What conclusions can we draw from these results?

p58.original: 你应该还记得，细胞因子除了充当“化学信使”外，还能引发某些特定的行为，如社交回避。因此，斯拉维奇的研究对于解释身体之外的社会应激源如何转化为生理改变，从而导致一些人罹患抑郁症等疾病的风险增加是有帮助的。
p58.en: As you will remember, in addition to acting as a “chemical courier”, cytogens can trigger certain specific behaviours, such as social evasiveness. Therefore, the Slavic study has been helpful in explaining how social stressors outside the body have been transformed into physical changes, leading to an increased risk of depression and other diseases.

p59.en: It's time to force the cell to age.

p60.original: 心理应激也会加速细胞的衰老，进而对身体健康产生影响。评估细胞老化的一种方法是测量其端粒（telomeres）的长度。图14-8阐述了该过程是如何发生的。在人的一生中，端粒会随着年龄的增长而缩短。然而，重要的是，端粒的长度与许多疾病有关，包括癌症、心血管疾病和糖尿病。最近的研究表明，端粒长度确实与早亡率相关（D’Mello et al.，2015；Wentzensen et al.，2011；Zhao et al.，2013）。
p60.en: Psychological stress also accelerates cell ageing, which in turn affects physical health. One way to assess cell ageing is to measure the length of its end particles (telomers). Figure 14-8 illustrates how this process happened. In a lifetime, the particles shrink with age. However, it is important that the length of the particles is associated with many diseases, including cancer, cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Recent studies have shown that the size of the particle is indeed associated with premature mortality (D'Mello et al., 2015); Wentzensen et al., 2011; Zhao et al., 2013).

p61.original: 在一项具有里程碑意义的研究中，心理学家埃利萨·埃佩尔（Elissa Epel）探讨了应激对端粒长度的影响，即母亲的细胞端粒长度是否与要照顾患有慢性病或感到压力的孩子有关。她发现，感知到的应激程度比仅仅暴露于应激环境中更重要。具体而言，高应激感知与免疫细胞的端粒缩短的速度有关（Epel et al.，2004）。仅仅作为一个照料者与细胞端粒长度变化无关，但应激情境的持续时间也很重要。孩子患病的时间越长，母亲的细胞端粒长度就越短。自这项研究以来，人们也越来越清楚，童年经历的强烈应激事件是导致细胞端粒变短的另一个罪魁祸首（Price et al.，2013）。
p61.en: In a landmark study, a psychologist, Elissa Epel, explored the effects of stress on the length of the pellets, i.e. whether the cytology of the mother was related to the care of a child suffering from chronic illness or stress. She found that perceived stress levels were more important than exposure only to stress environments. In particular, high stress perception is associated with the speed of reduction of the atoms in immunosupulation cells (Epel et al., 2004). As a caregiver alone, it is not related to changes in the size of the cytology, but it is also important to maintain the duration of the passion. The longer the child falls ill, the shorter the cytopellets of the mother. Since the study, it has also become increasingly clear that the strong stress events experienced in childhood are another cause of the smallness of cell particles (Price et al., 2013).

p62.original: 长期的或创伤性应激可能会影响我们如何看待日常应激事件，从而在一定程度上发挥作用。对威胁的认知评估、预期未来会发生不好的事情、悲观地看待自己，在某种程度上解释了应激与细胞端粒之间的关系。例如，认为有压力的实验任务更具有威胁性，或者对生活有更消极的预期（悲观程度）都与更短的细胞端粒长度相关（Ikeda et al.，2014；O’Donovan et al.，2009）。这一点非常重要，因为它表明认知评估在应激与疾病的关系中起着至关重要的作用。
p62.en: Long-term or traumatic stress may affect how we view day-to-day stress events and thus play a part. The cognitive assessment of the threat, the expectation of bad things in the future, and the pessimism of the self explain to some extent the relationship between stress and cell particles. For example, experimental missions that are perceived to be under stress are more threatening or have more negative expectations of life (pessimism) associated with shorter cytological particle lengths (Ikeda et al., 2014); O'Donovan et al., 2009. This is important because it shows that cognitive assessment plays a crucial role in the relationship between stress and disease.

p63.original: 图14-8 应激和生活方式会缩短细胞的寿命
p63.en: Figure 14-8: Stress and lifestyle reduce cell longevity

p64.original: 注：应激和生活方式会加速细胞的衰老或者与年龄有关的退化。
p64.en: Note: Stress and lifestyle can accelerate cell ageing or age-related degradation.

p65.original: 心理学很有用 对模糊威胁的认知评估
p65.en: Psychology is useful. A cognitive assessment of vague threats.

p66.original: 在“9·11”事件之后的几个月内，许多首批抵达现场的救援人员仍然在世贸中心展开搜救工作。当美国环境保护署（Environmental Protection Agency，EPA）的官员和纽约市市长宣布可以安全呼吸空气时，许多救援人员摘下了防护面罩。因为戴着面罩很闷热又影响视线。然而可以安全呼吸空气的公告真的准确吗？世贸中心的废墟还在冒烟，距离废墟1.6千米远的地方，约3厘米的灰尘覆盖在窗框上。试想一下飞机撞击并摧毁两座110层的大楼会产生怎样的后果。仔细检查现场的话，你觉得会发现什么？你能想象在地面环境如此不健康的情况下，美国环境保护署发布了如此积极的公告背后的心理原因是什么呢？
p66.en: In the months following the events of 11 September, many of the first rescue workers who arrived at the site were still in search and rescue at the World Trade Centre. When officials of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Mayor of New York City declared safe air breathing, many rescue workers removed their protective masks. I'm not sure if I'm going to be able to do this, but I'm going to do it. But is it true that the announcement of safe air breathing is accurate? The ruins of the World Trade Center are still smoked, 1.6 km away from the ruins, and about 3 centimetres of dust are covered in window frames. Imagine the consequences of an aircraft impacting and destroying two 110-storey buildings. If you check the scene carefully, what do you think you'll find? Can you imagine the psychological reasons behind such a positive announcement by the United States Environmental Protection Agency in such a unhealthy situation on the ground?

p67.original: “9·11”事件中双子塔倒塌后，许多首批抵达现场的救援人员在没有防护面罩保护的情况下，持续地在现场工作了几个月。
p67.en: Following the collapse of the twin towers in the events of 11 September, many of the first rescue workers who arrived at the site continued to work on the site for several months without the protection of their masks.

p68.original: 灾难发生大约10年后，《纽约时报》（New York Times，2011）发表了一篇关于“次生悲剧”的报告，即“9·11”事件对现场救援人员的健康造成的后续危害，由于政府官员宣称可以安全呼吸空气，导致救援人员撤消了防护措施，但事实上这么做是致命的。
p68.en: Some 10 years after the disaster, the New York Times (New York Times, 2011) published a report on the “second-life tragedy” of the follow-up damage to the health of relief workers on the ground as a result of the events of 11 September, which resulted in relief workers withdrawing their protective measures because government officials claimed to be safe to breathe air, but which was in fact fatal.

p69.original: 科学家们声称，2001年9月11日世贸中心被毁所释放出的烟雾、灰尘是纽约市有史以来最严重的环境灾难。温度高达1000度的大火产生的有毒烟雾笼罩着曼哈顿下城，并蔓延到邻近地区。倒塌的双子塔使得水泥和大楼中的其他东西变成了粉末，包括石棉。同时，楼层倒塌所产生的巨大压力将各种物质融合在一起，形成了科学家们以前从未见过的危险混合物。
p69.en: Scientists claim that the smoke and dust released by the destruction of the World Trade Center on 11 September 2001 were the worst environmental disaster in the history of New York City. The toxic smoke generated by a fire of up to 1,000 degrees covered the lower city of Manhattan and spread to adjacent areas. The collapse of the twin towers made cement and other building objects powdered, including asbestos. At the same time, the enormous pressure of the collapse of the floor has combined the substances into a dangerous mixture that scientists have never seen before.

p70.original: 据一些官员和医疗专家估计，在废墟上停留过的工作人员和志愿者总计有40000到90000人，他们可能都会在某种程度上受到灰尘的影响。在废墟上工作的9000多名人员对90家政府机构和公司提起诉讼，声称他们的疾病和损伤是由于现场作业造成的。
p70.en: Some officials and medical experts estimate that between 40,000 and 90,000 staff and volunteers have stayed on the ruins, and that they may all be affected to some extent by dust. More than 9,000 people working on the ruins have filed lawsuits against 90 government agencies and companies claiming that their illness and injuries resulted from on-site operations.

p71.original: 那么，当政府官员们宣称可以安全呼吸空气时，他们是在故意撒谎吗？你是怎么认为的？
p71.en: So, when government officials claim to be safe to breathe air, are they deliberately lying? What do you think?

p72.original: 假定他们应该意识到这种危险就体现了一种判断错误，这被称为事后偏差，类似于周一早上对前一天橄榄球比赛失误的分析。事后人们可能很容易得知当时救援人员面临着危险，但当时官员面临的是此前从未遭遇过的情境，对各种各样的预测感到无所适从。2011年在日本发生地震、海啸和核泄漏后的几天里，日本官方发布的乐观公告里也体现了类似的判断错误。
p72.en: Assuming that they should be aware of this danger, there is a judgement error, which is called an ex post facto deviation, similar to the analysis of the previous day's football error on Monday morning. It may be easy to know later that relief workers were at risk at the time, but officials were faced with situations that had never been experienced before and were dissatisfied with various predictions. A similar error of judgement was reflected in the optimistic announcement issued by the Japanese official in 2011, a few days after the earthquake, tsunami and nuclear spill in Japan.

p73.original: 我们还必须承认认知评估的力量。为了能对情境做出有效的认知评估，我们必须对威胁的性质有一个明确的认识。例如，毫无疑问，“9·11”事件的受害者经历了痛苦，意识到自己曾身处险境。但在袭击发生后的几年里，如果游客在乘坐飞机前看到政府的颜色预警系统显示恐怖主义威胁级别提高时，他们依然会感到不安。政府的预警系统是用来评估恐怖主义威胁级别并告知公众的，但这个系统给公众造成了困惑和不安。由于预警信息发布时正好是美国大选的日子，引发了公众不信任这一举动潜在的政治动机（Zimbardo，2004a），因此2011年该系统被废除了。关键在于：不确定性会增加人们对某一情境的应激。因此，解释或认知评估可以使一系列模糊威胁所累积的痛苦，在本质上与一次重大创伤性事件应激反应相同。
p73.en: We must also recognize the power of cognitive assessment. In order to be able to make an effective cognitive assessment of the situation, we must have a clear understanding of the nature of the threat. For example, there is no doubt that the victims of the events of 11 September have experienced suffering and are aware of the dangers they have faced. However, in the years following the attack, tourists would remain disturbed if they saw the Government's colour early warning system before flying on the air indicating an increase in the level of terrorist threat. The Government's early warning system, which was used to assess the level of terrorist threats and to inform the public, created confusion and anxiety among the public. The system was abolished in 2011 as the early warning message was released on the occasion of the United States general elections, which triggered public distrust of the underlying political motivations for the move (Zimbardo, 2004a). The key is that uncertainty increases stress in a given situation. Thus, interpretation or cognitive assessment can result in the accumulation of suffering from a series of vague threats, which is essentially the same as a major traumatic incident stress.
